clue.text: CO allegedly held back with hesitation

indicators.note: allegedly means 'so it is said', so what follows is only how the word sounds when spoken

parts.note: held back is docked, as pay is docked, and er is the noise of hesitation: docked with er

explanation.surface: A commanding officer, it is said, was kept back while dithering.
explanation.walkthrough: This puzzle's theme is the Carry On films, a long-running series of British comedy films, so CO stands for Carry On. DOCKED + ER, said aloud, gives the film title.
explanation.definitionFit: Carry On Doctor (1967) is one of the films in the British comedy series.

clue.text: Time for New Yorkers to eat load of French food

indicators.note: something that eats another takes it inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: EST is Eastern Standard Time, the time zone of New York
a cargo is a load carried by a ship or plane

explanation.surface: New Yorkers sit down at last to a big plate of French cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Escargots are snails cooked as a French delicacy, a classic dish of French cuisine.

clue.text: Neither thanks mass uprising for CO

indicators.note: in a down clue an uprising reads the pieces from the bottom upwards, so backwards

parts.note: neither is paired with nor, here standing in for it
ta is British informal for thanks
M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A commanding officer gets no gratitude when the masses rise up.
explanation.definitionFit: Carry On Matron (1972) is one of the films in the British comedy series.

clue.text: Stick around a little, because this is sweet

indicators.note: the first piece goes around the second, enclosing it

parts.note: glue is something that makes things stick, and to glue is to stick
cos is a shortened, little form of because

explanation.surface: Someone is told to linger a while because the occasion is a sweet one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little' tells you to shorten 'because' to its informal clipped form COS.
explanation.definitionFit: Glucose is a simple sugar, so it is literally sweet stuff.

clue.text: Reduce tension in defeat: a tyrant's leadership rejected across America

indicators.note: the first piece stretches across the second, holding it inside
rejected means these letters are thrown out of the word before it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so this takes the first letter of the word

parts.note: US is the United States of America

explanation.surface: Calm things down after a tyrant's leadership is defeated and spurned across America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a tyrant's leadership' is two things removed by 'rejected': the word a, and the tyrant's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To defuse a situation is to calm it, taking the heat or tension out of it.

clue.text: Article about riot appeared

indicators.note: about means going round, so the article surrounds the other piece

parts.note: an is the indefinite article in grammar
a rising is a riot or revolt

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about a riot has been published.
explanation.definitionFit: To have arisen is to have come up or emerged, a synonym of having appeared.

clue.text: Where prisoners eat CO

parts.note: cons is slang for convicts, prisoners
read with 'eat': where (prisoners) eat is a table, the place you sit to eat

explanation.surface: It reads like a quiz question about a prison canteen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Where' and 'eat' work as one phrase wrapped around 'prisoners', so the piece for prisoners comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Carry On Constable (1960) is one of the films in the British comedy series.

clue.text: CO appearing regularly in Schroedinger style

indicators.note: letters appearing at regular intervals: here every third letter is taken

explanation.surface: A commanding officer behaves in the spirit of Schroedinger's cat, both there and not there.
explanation.walkthrough: Take every third letter of SCHROEDINGERSTYLE: the 3rd, 6th, 9th, 12th and 15th.
explanation.definitionFit: Carry On Henry (1971), a romp about Henry VIII, is one of the films in the series.

clue.text: He made reptiles vanish, recreating past magic

indicators.note: recreating means creating again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a trick is a piece of magic

explanation.surface: A magician brings back old illusions, making reptiles disappear.
explanation.walkthrough: The ST is the abbreviation for Saint, and the (2,7) enumeration hints at it.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend says Saint Patrick drove all the snakes out of Ireland.

clue.text: First seen in Nightingale, undying resilience supporting each CO

indicators.note: first means take the first letter of each word that follows

explanation.surface: Florence Nightingale's tireless resilience underpins every commanding officer.
explanation.walkthrough: Florence Nightingale was the pioneer of modern nursing, so the surface already points at the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Carry On Nurse (1959) is one of the films in the British comedy series.

clue.text: See 14
Inhale from a smoking thing

definitions.meaning: to ... a cigarette is to inhale from it

explanation.definitionFit: Dragging on a cigarette means drawing smoke from it; a dragon is a beast that breathes out smoke.

clue.text: Strange, strange, strange: ultimately CO

indicators.note: strange means unusual, so the following word's letters are put in an unusual order
ultimately means at the end, so take the last letter

explanation.surface: Someone keeps repeating 'strange' before concluding about a commanding officer.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Strange' signals an anagram of the second plus E, the third's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Carry On Sergeant (1958) was the first film in the British comedy series.

clue.text: Reheats damaged part of wood?

indicators.note: damaged means broken, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Warming things up again has spoiled a piece of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A wood is made of trees, so one ash is an example of part of a wood; hence the query.

clue.text: See 17
Where there's a will there's way? Contest disputed, not won

indicators.note: disputed means argued over and so thrown into disorder, signalling a shuffle
not means the letters of the following word are left out of the mix

explanation.surface: A twist on the proverb, as heirs fight over a contested will.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffle WAY and CONTEST together, then take away the letters of WON.
explanation.definitionFit: Testacy is the legal state of having left a valid will at death, the opposite of intestacy.

clue.text: Boatman's origins in the arts reassessed

indicators.note: a word's origin is its beginning, so take the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: The setter Boatman's roots in the arts are being weighed up afresh.
explanation.walkthrough: Boatman is this puzzle's setter, but here the name is just a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Tar is old slang for a sailor, someone who works on boats.

clue.text: Admirer of oddly stupid, yet rugged, prominence

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters of the word

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, a rugged rise in the land, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A stupid man admires a craggy landmark.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky outcrop on a hilltop, typical of the moors of south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitor is a man who courts a woman, an admirer seeking her hand.

clue.text: CO manifested in muscle oxidation

indicators.note: manifested in means shown within, so the answer sits inside these words

explanation.surface: Carbon monoxide shows up when muscles oxidise, like a chemistry note.
explanation.walkthrough: CO looks like the chemical formula for carbon monoxide, fitting 'oxidation', but it is Carry On.
explanation.definitionFit: Carry On Cleo (1964), a send-up of Cleopatra, is one of the films in the series.

clue.text: Tories' top minister lacking means to gain goodwill for CO

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter
lacking means going without, so these letters are taken out

parts.note: a minister of religion is a preacher
PR, public relations, is the business of winning goodwill

explanation.surface: A Conservative minister lacks the spin needed to win goodwill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minister' here is a clergyman, not a government minister as the Tories suggest.
explanation.definitionFit: Carry On Teacher (1959) is one of the films in the British comedy series.

clue.text: Anonymous newspaper article uncovered abuse by CO

indicators.note: anonymous means without a name, so N for name is taken out

parts.note: a column is a regular article in a newspaper

indicators.note: uncovered means the outer letters are stripped away, leaving the middle

explanation.surface: An unsigned newspaper piece exposed abuse by a commanding officer.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the abbreviation for name; COLUMN without it is COLUM, then BUS from inside abuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Carry On Columbus (1992) was a late entry in the British comedy film series.

clue.text: Carry on making endless profits

indicators.note: endless means without its final letter

parts.note: proceeds are the money made from a sale, the profits

explanation.surface: Keep going and make money without end.
explanation.walkthrough: In a puzzle where CO means Carry On, here the phrase is literal: it means continue.
explanation.definitionFit: To proceed is to go on with something, to continue.

clue.text: Perhaps Cape Fear, Fahrenheit dropped after cold closes in

indicators.note: after means this piece comes after the one before in the answer
cold closes in: the word for cold closes around the word in, enclosing it

parts.note: raw weather is cold and damp

indicators.note: dropped means this letter is left out of the word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Cape Fear is a thriller film, with the temperature falling as the cold sets in.
explanation.walkthrough: Cape Fear is a well-known film, but 'Perhaps Cape' is the definition: RA(IN)W then EAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A cape is a sleeveless cloak, one example of clothing worn against the rain.

clue.text: Not a major route to CO

definitions.meaning: in Britain A roads are the major routes: read as a phrase
Carry On, the theme's film series

explanation.definitionFit: Carry On Abroad (1972), a package-holiday farce, is a film in the series; minor British roads are classed B.

clue.text: Drink coming up with Spooner in the vicinity

indicators.note: Spooner was famous for swapping the first sounds of words, so swap the opening sounds of these two

parts.note: beer is a drink
nigh means close at hand, coming up soon

explanation.surface: A drink appears as the Reverend Spooner arrives in the neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of BEER NIGH gives 'near by'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearby means close at hand, near the place mentioned.

clue.text: Boatman follows core of convoluted book

indicators.note: follows means this piece comes after the one before in the answer
the core of a word is what is left once its outer layers are stripped away

parts.note: taken as written
the setter, Boatman, refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: The setter tracks the heart of a tangled book.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often stand for ME, here by their pseudonym, Boatman.
explanation.definitionFit: A volume is a book, especially one of a set.

clue.text: Struggle with editor's extremes in the Spectator

parts.note: to vie is to compete, to struggle against

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An editor at The Spectator, a British political weekly, fights at both extremes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Spectator' looks like the magazine, but the definition is just one who watches.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator is a person who watches, which is what a viewer does.

clue.text: Sad lament for inherited status

indicators.note: sad in the sense of sorry or in a poor state, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mournful dirge laments the burden of an inherited position.
explanation.definitionFit: To take on someone's mantle is to inherit their role or authority, from Elijah's cloak passing to Elisha.

clue.text: About to tuck into sourdough!

indicators.note: tucking into something means going inside it, so one piece is put inside

parts.note: milk that goes bad turns sour
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A cheerful cry before biting into a sourdough loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sourdough' must be split into sour (BAD) and dough, which is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread and dough are both slang for money, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: CO scaring me in a funny way

indicators.note: something done in a funny way is done oddly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A commanding officer frightens me with a strange manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Carry On Screaming (1966), a horror spoof, is one of the films in the series.

clue.text: Bad-tempered Republican leader ejected by CO

indicators.note: ejected means thrown out, so this letter is removed

parts.note: crabby means grumpy, bad-tempered

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so take the first letter

explanation.surface: A grumpy Republican leader is thrown out by a commanding officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Carry On Cabby (1963), about rival taxi firms, is one of the films in the series.

clue.text: Even cycling finds unexpected zeal around united country

indicators.note: cycling moves the letters round, from one end to the other
the rearranged letters go around the next piece
unexpected means surprising, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cycling race uncovers surprising passion around a united nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves the first letter of Even to its end; 'unexpected' scrambles zeal, and 'around' puts that round U.
explanation.definitionFit: Venezuela is a country in South America.
